intro.heads_up: Quick heads-up before we dive in: by the time this episode drops Tuesday morning, Patch 12.1.5 is going live in North America, Kith'ix and the Labyrinths are here, and Europe gets it Wednesday.
rundown: Forever beta week four: Dalaran opens up, XP goes up, and Classic looting comes back
a big round of Forever class fixes, with rage finally getting sorted out
Holly Longdale's PAX Aus keynote and our first real look at a brand-new Forever dungeon
Clay Stone on horizontal progression, the item squish, and a regional GDKP ban
the road to launch: beta ending, name reservation, and gold buyers
everything landing in Midnight's 12.1.5 on October 13
and we'll close out the news with Zul'Aman for the TBC Anniversary realms and a quick look at ThugUI

items.title: Forever Beta: The October 8 Build
items.synopsis: The October 8 build opened the City of Dalaran dungeon, sped up dungeon leveling, and brought back a few Classic behaviors players had been asking for.
points: Blizzard calling it Week 4: team up and take on the City of Dalaran, up to level 30
the brand-new City of Dalaran dungeon now open for testing
experience from dungeon kills going up about 20%

points.sub: XP now depends only on your own level, the same as Classic Era

points: Classic looting back: mobs that dropped nothing can still be interacted with
weapon-swap macros working inside the same GCD again
every beta player getting the Legacy Challenge completion: 16 Legacy Points
Cooldown Manager now supporting every class, racial, and trinket, with consumables coming later
a Discord Voice option under Audio, and Group Finder able to prompt your group into voice chat
more gamepad work: the gamepad action bar now supports Edit Mode
Will of the Forsaken usable while asleep or charmed again
Blizzard's own 'LF1M for boar killing' post pulling about 34,000 likes: the hype is real
questions: Dalaran finally playable. Is a new dungeon in a city everyone knows the most exciting thing in this build, or is it the XP bump?
Built-in Discord voice in the Group Finder. Would you actually use that in pugs?

items.title: Forever Class Changes: Rage Gets Fixed
items.synopsis: The same build carried a long list of class fixes, led by a rage rework and a push to put several abilities back to their Vanilla values.

points.sub: it was using your health instead of the creature's, mishandling crits, and counting absorbs

points: rage gains now rebalanced to 20% to 40% depending on level
Bear and Dire Bear threat bonus up to 50%, and Mana Potions usable in Bear, Dire Bear, and Cat Form
Druid Thorns and Paladin Retribution Aura damage going back to Vanilla values, about a third less
Discipline Penance nerfed after a bug left it channeling for 3 seconds instead of 2
Survival's Expose Prey doubled to 10 seconds, and Entrapment now has diminishing returns
Arms Warriors needing Deep Wounds again to reach Impale
Protection Warriors' Last Stand giving the right amount of health again
Warlock pets now stunned while you summon a new one
lots of low-rank spells retuned for smoother growth: Frostbolt, Fireball, Smite, Lightning Bolt, Shadow Bolt
questions: The rage fix touches every Warrior and Bear. Does this change how you feel about the Warrior cleave king talk from last week?
Blizzard is pulling some numbers back to Vanilla. Should Forever stick close to the old values, or keep its own tuning?

sources.label: Blizzard, WoW: Forever Beta Development Notes (October 8 update)

items.title: PAX Aus: Holly's Keynote and Krol'dok Stronghold
items.category: World of Warcraft: Forever, PAX Aus 2026
items.synopsis: Holly Longdale opened PAX Aus with her Storytime keynote, and Clay Stone gave the first real behind-the-scenes look at a brand-new Forever dungeon, Krol'dok Stronghold.

points.text: Krol'dok Stronghold: a level 40 to 45 Twilight's Hammer ogre fortress
points.sub: in the new Riverglades zone on the eastern coast of the Eastern Kingdoms, near Redridge and the Burning Steppes

points: the dungeon starting as a gnoll idea and turning into ogres, because gnolls were already everywhere in Vanilla
a vertical climb over bridges that ends at the summit: rerouted after playtests so you never walk back down
a big hole in one bridge left in on purpose and made canon, because they're ogres
five ogre bosses shown, including a two-headed ogre with a purple crystal and a woman with wolves
Clay walking through the original pitch: the world is the main character, journey before destination, protect the social experience
not a remake, no art-style overhaul, and nothing that stomps on later lore
Forever pitched as the permanent third pillar of WoW, with frequent big updates
lessons from China's Reforged realms going straight into Forever
Holly's path from EverQuest dark elf to running all of Warcraft
her line that once a game ships, it belongs to the community
Holly calling this the biggest beta Blizzard has ever run
no new systems or date changes, still level 60 and November 4
questions: An ogre fortress you climb from the bottom to the top. Does Krol'dok sound like the kind of new dungeon that earns a spot next to the originals?
Holly says the game belongs to the community once it ships. Does Forever feel more like that than retail does right now?

items.title: Clay Stone on Progression, GDKP, and the Squish
items.category: World of Warcraft: Forever, Developer Interviews
items.synopsis: In interviews around PAX, Clay Stone explained what horizontal progression actually means for Forever, and that the GDKP ban only covers North America and Europe.
points: horizontal progression meaning more content and more world, not gear that stops going up
small gear upgrades between raids, with power increases handled carefully
no full item squish or reset decided yet

points.text: the GDKP ban only applying to North America and Europe
points.sub: a regional rule, not a worldwide one

points: the economy lessons from earlier Classic realms shaping Forever's rules
the camping system landing well, and devs already talking about expanding it
the community split, some happy with the economy talk, some saying tier 2 beating tier 1 is still just vertical
questions: If tier 2 is still better than tier 1, is horizontal progression just a new name for the old treadmill?
GDKP banned here but not elsewhere. Does a regional ban actually stop it, or just push it to Discord?

items.title: The Road to Launch: Beta End, Names, and Gold-Buyer Bans
items.synopsis: With the beta wrapping up October 21 and launch on November 4, Blizzard laid out how early name reservation works while it keeps closing gold-buying accounts.
points: beta testing ending October 21, and none of your beta progress carries over
early name reservation running October 27 through November 3

points.text: reservation only for players who bought an upgrade
points.sub: the Skyborne Heroic Pack, Skyborne Epic Pack, or Warcraft Forever Collection: a beta invite alone doesn't count

points: up to three characters per account, fully customized ahead of time
no realms means every name has to be unique across the whole region
characters getting both a first and a second name
no early access: everyone starts November 4
the gold-buyer ban totals Aggrend gave earlier, more than 2,100 buyers, nearly 4,000 RMT closures in total
a new trade warning coming for gold trades and mail from people you don't know
questions: Region-wide unique names with a first and last name. Does that save the name-ban mess, or just move it?
Banning gold buyers instead of only sellers. Is that the right line, or will innocent people get caught?

items.title: Midnight 12.1.5 Arrives October 13
items.synopsis: Patch 12.1.5 lands October 13 in North America and October 14 in Europe with the one-boss Kith'ix raid, the Labyrinths, class tuning, and a big round of housing decor changes.
points: The Unbinding of Kith'ix: a focused one-boss raid in Story, Raid Finder, Normal, Heroic, and Mythic
Mythic Kith'ix running as flexible 15-to-25-player groups
the Labyrinth of Kindo'jan arriving alongside it
major class tuning in the patch: Devourer and Void-Scarred Demon Hunter getting the biggest list

points.text: the October 6 hotfixes already landing ahead of it
points.sub: six PvE specs including an Unholy nerf, a pile of PvP changes, and a long list of Ula'tek nerfs

points: crafted decor needing a lot less lumber across the board
the Apothecary's Worktable going from 8 Black Lotus down to 1
a batch of new craftable decor sending you back through Oribos, Dalaran, Boralus, Dazar'alor, and Nazjatar
Hallow's End spooky decor available for your house right now
questions: A one-boss raid with flex Mythic. Is that a good fit for the guild, or a weird tier to pace a team around?
Ula'tek nerfs right before a new raid. Does that change our plan for the week?

items.title: TBC Anniversary Phase 3.5: Zul'Aman
items.synopsis: The Burning Crusade Anniversary realms get Phase 3.5 on October 22, opening Zul'Aman and making the old raids much easier to catch up on.
points: Phase 3.5 going live October 22 at 3pm Pacific
Gods of Zul'Aman: the 10-player troll raid in the Ghostlands
the hostage timer run: save them all in time for the Amani War Bear
Hyjal and Black Temple attunements gone
Heroic dungeons getting easier, and Heroic keys needing only Honored now
Badges of Justice dropping from every raid boss, Karazhan through Zul'Aman
Kazzak and Doomwalker loot turning Bind on Equip
epic gems coming from Magtheridon's Black Sack of Gems and Jewelcrafters' Brilliant Glass
all landing two weeks before Forever launches, after last week's TBC raider numbers
questions: Is a Zul'Aman timer run enough to keep TBC raiders from leaving for Forever?
Did either of you ever get the Amani War Bear back in the day?

items.title: ThugUI: My Addon
items.synopsis: A quick look at ThugUI, the UI suite I build for Retail and WoW Forever.
points: one download for Retail and WoW Forever
every part a module you switch on or off
mouse and keyboard or controller, same features on both
cooldown grids and rings anchored to your cursor
health and resource orbs, party frames, and name-only nameplates
the controller wheel on Start for WoW Forever
Season of Thuggery: the Retail seasonal panel for your alts' gear and raid progress
find it on CurseForge or GitHub, and bring feedback to the Last Attempt Discord
questions: What would you want a UI addon to do for Forever that Blizzard's UI doesn't?
Controller players: is the wheel the thing that makes Forever playable on a pad?
